page: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-32xCPU-192GB is a Cloud Native family virtual server running on the KVM hypervisor. It features 32 shared vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC 7542 processor with an x86_64 architecture and a clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The system is equipped with 192.0 GB of system memory, yielding 6.0 GB of RAM per core. No local storage or GPU hardware is bundled with this instance, though it includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark data reveals a clear contrast between single-core and multi-core capabilities. Single-core performance is limited, with stress-ng single-core CPU performance scoring in the bottom 10% and bzip3 single-threaded decompression rated as weak. However, multi-core execution is highly effective, as demonstrated by a strong top 25% rating in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and average middle 50% scores across Geekbench multi-core, PassMark CPU, and stress-ng multi-core tests. Memory bandwidth remains stable in the average tier, reaching 125.11 GB/sec for large-block read operations.

The shared CPU allocation presents a performance tradeoff, making this server less suitable for sustained, latency-sensitive single-threaded tasks. However, the high resource density of 192.0 GB RAM combined with 32 vCPUs offers qualitative cost efficiency for multi-threaded workloads that can tolerate shared CPU capacity. This configuration is well-suited for parallel processing tasks, multi-threaded software compilation, database operations, and static web serving.
